title: She said she would come
goal: Report statements, questions and requests without quoting them, and follow a message passed on.

intro.text: Report a statement with `-dYgY`, the possessive and the accusative before *aýtmak*: *Ertir geljekdigini aýtdy*, he said he would come tomorrow. A question keeps its question word and takes *soramak*. A request takes the verbal noun: *Meniň gelmegimi haýyş etdi*, she asked me to come.

vocab.en: to ask, to request (sizden haýyş edýärin: I ask you)
to order, to tell (someone to do something)

exercises.question: *Aýna ertir geljekdigini aýtdy.* What did Aýna say?

why.1: **Come** would be a request: *gelmegimi haýyş etdi*. *Geljekdigini* is a statement about the future.
why.2: *-jak* is the future: *geljekdigini*, that she would come.

exercises.en: Merdan said he lived in Ashgabat.

reject.why: Before *aýtmak*, the clause is the object: it takes the accusative, *-dygyny*.
*-dygymy* would be **that I lived**. It is Merdan's statement: *-dygyny*.

exercises.prompt: He said he would come tomorrow.

reject.why: *Gelendigini* is **that he came**. For **would come**, use the future: *geljekdigini*.

exercises.explain: The future *geljek*, then *-digini* (that he…, as an object), then *aýtdy*.

accept: He asked where I was going.
She asked where I was going
[He|She] asked me where I was going

exercises.label: *gelmek*, that … will come, as an object: that I will come, that you will come…
exercises.explain: *geljek* + *-dig* + the possessive + the accusative: *geljekdigimi aýtdym*, I said I would come.

exercises.question: Aýna said, *“Men ýadaw.”* How do you report it?

why.1: *Ýadawdygymy* would be **that I was tired**, you who are reporting.

exercises.explain: Aýna speaks about herself: *-dygyny*, her own. The tense stays present.

reject.why: A request takes the verbal noun, *gelmegimi*, not the fact clause *gelendigimi*.

exercises.prompt: The teacher told us to open our books.

accept: My mother told me to come early.
My [mum|mom] told me to come early

exercises.question: He asked me, **“Where do you live?”** Which report is right?

why.1: A question is reported with *soramak*. *Aýtdy* would mean he told someone where I lived.
why.2: The question was about me: *ýaşaýandygymy*, where I lived.

exercises.explain: The question word stays inside, the clause has my possessive, and the verb is *sorady*.

exercises.prompt: I asked her when she would come.
exercises.explain: The person asked in the ablative, *ondan*; the question word *haçan* stays in the clause.

accept: My father told me not to be late.
My [father|dad] ordered me not to be late
My dad told me not to be late

exercises.prompt: Let me know if you're coming.
exercises.explain: *habar bermek*: to let someone know, with the person in the dative, *maňa*. A plan takes *bolsa* after a participle: *geljek bolsaň*.

exercises.title: Ejemiň jaňy
exercises.passage:
Ejem jaň etdi. Ol ertir agşam Marydan geljekdigini aýtdy. Otly sagat altyda gelýär. Ejem Batyryň ony wokzalda garşylamagyny haýyş etdi.

Ejem ýene bir zat aýtdy: daýzamyz kesel eken, şonuň üçin ol bir hepde Maryda galypdyr. Ol daýzamyzyň indi kesel däldigini aýtdy.

Iň soňunda ejem: “Öýi arassalaň!” diýdi. Men öýi arassalajakdygymyzy aýtdym. Batyr bolsa: “Ejem garaşmasyn diýip, wokzala ir bararyn” diýdi.
exercises.translation: Mum called. She said she would be coming from Mary tomorrow evening. The train arrives at six. Mum asked Batyr to meet her at the station. Mum said one more thing: our aunt had been ill, it turns out, so she stayed in Mary for a week. She said our aunt was no longer ill. Finally Mum said, “Clean the house!” I said we would clean the house. And Batyr said, “I'll go to the station early, so that Mum doesn't have to wait.”

questions.explain: *Ertir agşam … geljekdigini aýtdy. Otly sagat altyda gelýär.*

questions.q: What did Mum ask Batyr to do?
Why will Batyr go to the station early?
options: so that Mum won't have to wait
questions.explain: *Ejem garaşmasyn diýip*: so that Mum doesn't wait.
